niche: Strange true stories from aviation history: early flight pioneers, WW1 and WW2 pilots, record attempts, impossible survivals, odd inventions and planes that changed everything, told through one pilot or aircraft at the center (pre-1990 events with real archival photos; no modern airline crashes or cockpit recordings, no graphic deaths, nothing political)
audience: Curious viewers aged 18 to 54, mainly in the US, UK, Canada and Australia, who like planes, WW2 history, military documentaries and adventure stories, and watch Shorts while scrolling
tone: Like a friend telling a gripping story at a bar: it opens in the cockpit at the strangest moment, moves fast as one flowing story where every beat leads to the next (but / so / you see), with concrete details such as altitudes, dates and names and a dry wit, and saves the answer or twist for the very last line, which makes people rewatch or comment
